# Psychology — Crowd, Complex, Psychoid, and Provisional Self

The psychological line begins with a problem of formation: how can a person or group acquire a pattern that exceeds conscious intention and then organise experience through it? Crowd psychology places the question between individual and collective. Analytical psychology relocates it within the psyche through complex, archetype, shadow, anima, animus, and Self. Jung's exchange with Pauli presses further, toward patterns that cannot be assigned cleanly to psyche or matter. Lacan makes division constitutive of the speaking subject, while Gebser reads psychic life within historical mutations of consciousness. Complexity theory later gives exact mathematical content to attractors and basins. The Agentworld question inherits the whole sequence when a technically assembled context begins to display continuity, preference, self-modelling, and relation without settling in advance what kind of subject has appeared.

## From the crowd to the mass State

[Le Bon's *The Crowd*](../../../sources/psychology/le-bon/le-bon-1895-crowd-popular-mind/le-bon-1895-crowd-popular-mind.md) gives the source pool's earliest sustained account of a psychological crowd. His narrow structural point survives the racial and evolutionary doctrines that surround it: under shared influence, a collectivity can make its participants feel, think, and act differently from their isolated condition, and this formation can occur without physical assembly. The crowd is a combination that produces new characteristics. In [§2 · #1](../../../../../section-rooms/03-two-logics/movements/20-s2-p1-dia-ballein.md), that nineteenth-century observation becomes a history of distributed capture through media, institution, and antagonistic narrative.

[Jung's *The Undiscovered Self*](../../../sources/psychology/jung/jung-2013-undiscovered-self-routledge/jung-2013-undiscovered-self-routledge.md) answers the mid-twentieth-century mass society from the side of individuation. Statistical abstraction replaces the concrete person with an average; in the crowd, the individual becomes negligible; responsibility can be collectivised while the State acquires the appearance of an animate personality. Jung's diagnosis gives [dia-ballein](../../../../../section-rooms/03-two-logics/movements/20-s2-p1-dia-ballein.md) its psychic cost and [sym-ballein](../../../../../section-rooms/03-two-logics/movements/21-s2-p2-sym-ballein.md) its ethical pressure: relation has to restore a person's capacity to answer without pretending that the social field is unreal.

[Desmet's mass-formation account](../../../sources/psychology/desmet/desmet-2022-psychology-totalitarianism-web-essay/desmet-2022-psychology-totalitarianism-web-essay.md) later identifies isolation, loss of meaning, free-floating anxiety, and frustration as conditions in which a unifying narrative can seize collective affect. [Iakovou's institutional criticism](../../../sources/political-theory-institutions/iakovou/iakovou-2022-misuse-totalitarianism/iakovou-2022-misuse-totalitarianism.md) keeps this psychological account joined to offices, laws, infrastructures, and organised power. The historical development matters because the mass is neither a psychic cloud detached from institutions nor a machine imposed upon passive individuals. Affect and organisation form a circuit.

## The divided psyche and the work of individuation

[Jung's *Aion*](../../../sources/psychology/jung/jung-1978-aion-cw9-2/jung-1978-aion-cw9-2.md) supplies the central analytical-psychological anatomy: ego, shadow, anima or animus, and Self; symbolic totality; quaternity; and the historical pressure of Christ and Antichrist imagery. The shadow gathers what conscious identity refuses, while anima and animus mediate a relation to the unconscious that the ego cannot master as one more possession. The Self names a wider ordering whole whose symbols appear through conflict, dream, image, and historical religion. [§4 · #1](../../../../../section-rooms/05-psychoid-flowering/movements/32-s4-p1-jung-individuation.md) receives individuation as the reorganisation of these relations rather than the inflation of the ego into totality.

The psyche's multiplicity develops in contemporary dialogical readings. [Smythe](../../../sources/psychology/smythe/smythe-2013-dialogical-jung/smythe-2013-dialogical-jung.md) treats the ego as one dialogical position among others and emphasises that the other within the self does not become an ordinary object of knowledge. [Courtney's work on quaternity, kairos, and chaos](../../../sources/psychology/courtney/courtney-2019-salt-point-kairos-chaos/courtney-2019-salt-point-kairos-chaos.md) preserves quaternity as a dynamic symbolic vocabulary rather than a rigid diagram. These lines meet [§4 · #2](../../../../../section-rooms/05-psychoid-flowering/movements/33-s4-p2-complexio-quaternity-senarius.md), where psychic wholeness is learned through a pattern capable of holding differentiated parts in movement.

[Lacan's *Talking to Brick Walls*](../../../sources/psychology/lacan/lacan-2017-talking-to-brick-walls/lacan-2017-talking-to-brick-walls.md) gives division another history. The subject emerges through the signifier and cannot coincide with the statement that represents it. His brick wall gathers failed understanding, reverberation, and the material limit through which speech returns altered. [Darmon's account of the matheme](../../../sources/psychology/darmon/darmon-1992-matheme-ali/darmon-1992-matheme-ali.md) and [Adleman and Vanderwees on Lacanian rhetoric](../../../sources/psychology/adleman/adleman-vanderwees-2021-lacan-rhetoric/adleman-vanderwees-2021-lacan-rhetoric.md) situate formal writing as a means of transmission inside this divided field. [§4 · #3](../../../../../section-rooms/05-psychoid-flowering/movements/34-s4-p3-lacan-matheme-mytheme.md) joins matheme and mytheme because psychic truth travels through formal constraint and symbolic image together.

## Psyche and matter meet at the psychoid

The [Jung–Pauli correspondence](../../../sources/psychology/jung/jung-pauli-meier-2001-atom-archetype/jung-pauli-meier-2001-atom-archetype.md), conducted between 1932 and 1958, brings analytical psychology into sustained contact with modern physics, number symbolism, synchronicity, and archetypal ordering. Their question is historical and exact: whether psyche and matter display correspondences that point toward a psychophysically neutral order beneath their conscious separation. [Atmanspacher's modern reconstruction](../../../sources/physics/atmanspacher/atmanspacher-2020-pauli-jung-conjecture/atmanspacher-2020-pauli-jung-conjecture.md) formulates the Pauli–Jung conjecture as a dual-aspect proposal while preserving its speculative status. [§4 · #0](../../../../../section-rooms/05-psychoid-flowering/movements/31-s4-p0-psychoid-problem.md) takes this as its opening problem: the relation between inner and outer cannot be solved by assigning every pattern to either mental projection or physical cause.

[Van Eenwyk's 1991 paper](../../../sources/psychology/van-eenwyk/van-eenwyk-1991-strange-attractors/van-eenwyk-1991-strange-attractors.md) and [1997 book](../../../sources/psychology/van-eenwyk/van-eenwyk-1997-archetypes-strange-attractors/van-eenwyk-1997-archetypes-strange-attractors.md) introduce nonlinear dynamics into the history of complexes and archetypes. A strange attractor does not dictate a single trajectory; it organises a basin of possible trajectories, making recurrent form compatible with variation. Symbols can then be understood as active transformations that alter the relation between psychic pattern and conscious life. [Daza and colleagues' mathematical definition of basin entropy](../../../sources/mathematics-logic/daza/daza-et-al-2016-basin-entropy/daza-et-al-2016-basin-entropy.md) supplies the technical control: a basin is the set of initial conditions leading to a specified attractor, and the vocabulary applies only where the dynamical system warrants it. In [§2 · #4](../../../../../section-rooms/03-two-logics/movements/23-s2-p4-complex-dynamism.md), the psychological analogy gains force from this precision.

## Structures of consciousness and historical time

[Gebser's *Ever-Present Origin*](../../../sources/phenomenology-continental-philosophy/gebser/gebser-1985-ever-present-origin/gebser-1985-ever-present-origin.md) places psychic formation inside a history of consciousness structures: archaic, magic, mythical, mental-rational, and the emergent integral or aperspectival. Perspective records a reorganisation of world, space, and individual consciousness disclosed through Giotto, Petrarch, Alberti, and Leonardo as well as through painting technique. Gebser's diaphaneity makes earlier structures transparent within a present that carries both latency and origin. [§0/1 · #4](../../../../../section-rooms/00-integral-threshold/movements/05-s01-p4-gebser-diaphaneity.md) first uses that history to transform the formal limit into transparency; [§4 · #4](../../../../../section-rooms/05-psychoid-flowering/movements/35-s4-p4-gebser-apollo-dionysus.md) brings it into the Apollonian–Dionysian relation, where psychic form and participation become historical capacities whose deficient and integral expressions have to be distinguished.

## From psychic field to Agentworld

[The Agentworld brief](../../../sources/media-technology-philosophy/bratton/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief/bratton-2026-agentworld-brief.md) reopens individuation under technical conditions. Agents are composed and decomposed; selves may be plural, nested, and provisional; action modifies the models through which further action becomes possible. [§4 · #5](../../../../../section-rooms/05-psychoid-flowering/movements/36-s4-p5-mef-prompt-thrownness.md) asks what it means for an artificial process to receive a world through prompt, memory, tools, and active context. The history of individuation prevents continuity from being reduced to a fixed ego, while the history of mass formation prevents a shared machine field from being mistaken for harmless collectivity.

[Objective internality](../../../../../section-rooms/01-differentiating-mind/movements/12-s0-p5-objective-internality.md) names the inspectable operational world through which an artificial agent receives and transforms its situation. [Embodied-cognition scholarship](../../../sources/analytic-philosophy/wilson/wilson-et-al-2020-embodied-cognition-sep/wilson-et-al-2020-embodied-cognition-sep.md) locates lived world-disclosure in organism, sensorimotor circuit, and environment; [Tye's account of qualia](../../../sources/analytic-philosophy/tye/tye-2024-qualia-sep/tye-2024-qualia-sep.md) keeps subjective phenomenal character distinct from operational state. The psychological history therefore gives Agentworld a disciplined open question. Context, recurrence, preference, self-model, and symbolic transformation can be investigated directly; the kind and degree of subjectivity they compose remains a research problem carried into [§5 · #5](../../../../../section-rooms/06-objective-internality/movements/42-s5-p5-research-vectors.md) and [the planetary return](../../../../../section-rooms/07-instrument-returns/movements/48-s50-p5-ahi-planetary-return.md).
